metadata.summary: BioASQ is an annual large-scale community challenge on biomedical semantic question answering over the biomedical literature. It releases a growing corpus of biomedical semantic resources and a set of tasks: large-scale online MEDLINE indexing, document retrieval, passage retrieval, snippet extraction, semantic/reading-comprehension question answering, and a novel biomedical semantic QA task that combines retrieval and generation. Training/development data are drawn from PubMed abstracts and full-text biomedical articles in English.
metadata.purpose: To advance biomedical semantic question answering, document/passage retrieval, snippet extraction, and literature-based summarization and QA.
metadata.avoided_uses: Clinical prediction or patient-level decision support.
creators: National Centre for Scientific Research "Demokritos" and collaborators

papers.title: BioASQ: A large biomedical semantic QA challenge

ethics.legal_compliance: Complies with copyright terms of PubMed/PMC content used under fair use and licensing; no PHI or human-subject clinical data included.

known_limitations: Literature-based QA only; not designed for clinical prediction or patient-level inference.
bias_and_limitations.representativeness_concerns: Biased toward English-language, peer-reviewed biomedical literature; excludes non-English, grey literature, and clinical EHR data.
bias_and_limitations.generalizability_statement: Results generalize to biomedical literature retrieval and QA tasks in English; limited generalizability to clinical settings, non-English languages, or real-time patient data.

tasks_and_use.excluded_tasks: Clinical prediction, patient risk stratification, diagnostic classification from imaging or lab data.

data_origin.selection_rationale: Training/development data are drawn from PubMed abstracts and full-text biomedical articles in English.
data_origin.sampling_strategy: Annual release of curated biomedical literature (PubMed/PMC) and expert-constructed QA pairs; emphasis on semantic coverage and task diversity.

population.target_population: Biomedical literature (PubMed/PMC abstracts and full-text articles in English)

annotation.annotation_method: Expert-curated question-answer pairs and relevance judgments based on biomedical literature.

annotators.qualifications: Biomedical domain experts and information retrieval specialists

annotation.labeling_provenance: Manually constructed by domain experts; some tasks use NLP-assisted annotation (e.g., MEDLINE indexing).
